then.text: How's the post office? Is it still the world's most southerly? We checked. It is. We're quite put out.
Off you go, then. East. Wait: west. We did move the station inland. Not that you can tell.
He's finally let go of the mail! The glaciologist's been sitting on it for a month, refusing to sign until someone beat him. Now someone has. Thank you. Here's the sack, and the signature.

else.text: Sign your sack? I can't. The glaciologist is holding the stamp, on the ice, outside, and he won't sign until someone beats him in a fair fight. It's a Halley thing. Go on.
Halley VI. We sit on a floating ice shelf, in the dark for months, and measure the sky. It was here, in the mid-80s, that British scientists first spotted the hole in the ozone layer.
It's mended a bit. It took a treaty, a lot of fridges and a lot of nerds with instruments. Which is the best ending of any story I know.
